chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the young girl who does not menstruate like her, and the one who has despaired of menstruation, he said: There is no waiting period (iddah) upon her, even if intercourse occurs with her.
ai.seo_question: What is the iddah (waiting period) for a woman who does not menstruate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that the obligation of 'iddah (waiting period) is contingent upon the occurrence of menstruation; thus, pre-pubescent girls and menopausal women are exempt even if consummation occurs. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'iddah serves primarily to ascertain paternity in cases of potential pregnancy, a condition absent in these two age groups. The narration underscores the practical application of Quranic verses on divorce by linking the legal requirement directly to biological markers rather than the act of marriage itself.
